title: Build a legal, transparent web-based parental control dashboard (Parent/Child/Admin)

requirements.text: Implement Internet Identity sign-in and role-based access (Parent, Child, Admin) for the web app, with clear navigation separation for each role.
acceptanceCriteria: Users can sign in using Internet Identity.
Backend stores a user profile keyed by Principal with an assigned role (Parent/Child/Admin).
Non-admin users cannot access Admin routes/APIs; Child users cannot access Parent-only routes/APIs.
UI shows role-appropriate entry points (e.g., Parent dashboard, Child check-in, Admin panel).

requirements.text: Create an onboarding flow for Parent–Child pairing using an invite code generated by the Parent and redeemed by the Child, including explicit consent and supervision disclosures.
acceptanceCriteria: Parent can generate a time-limited invite code for a specific Child profile.
Child can enter the invite code to link their account to the Parent.
Before linking completes, Child must confirm a consent checkbox acknowledging supervision and data sharing.
After pairing, Parent sees the linked Child in their dashboard; Child sees the linked Parent and supervision notice.

requirements.text: Provide a Parent dashboard to manage each linked Child: view summary cards, configure schedules/time limits, and review activity/location entries with transparency labels indicating data is child-submitted/consented.
acceptanceCriteria: Parent dashboard lists all linked Children with status (last check-in time, alerts count).
Selecting a Child opens tabs/sections for: Activity, Schedules & Limits, Content Filters, Location, Alerts, Audit Log.
All activity/location views show a clear label that data is provided through consented reporting (no hidden monitoring).

requirements.text: Implement scheduling and time-limit configuration for each Child (e.g., allowed hours by day, daily screen-time target), stored in the backend and editable only by the Parent (and Admin for support).
acceptanceCriteria: Parent can set allowed time windows per weekday and a daily usage limit value.
Backend validates and persists schedule settings per Child.
Child view can see the current schedule/limits in read-only form (transparency).

requirements.text: Implement a Child 'Check-in' area for submitting activity entries (app/site used, duration, notes) and optional location entries, with explicit per-entry consent and visibility into what will be shared.
acceptanceCriteria: Child can add an activity entry with required fields (label/category + duration) and optional details.
Child can add a location entry (textual place name and/or coordinates) with an explicit consent checkbox per submission.
Parent can view submitted entries chronologically; Child can view their own submission history.

requirements.text: Add configurable content filter settings per Child as a policy configuration UI (categories + allowlist/blocklist), stored in backend and displayed transparently to the Child as rules (without attempting device-level enforcement).
acceptanceCriteria: Parent can configure categories (e.g., 'Adult', 'Gambling', 'Violence') as allowed/blocked and maintain allowlist/blocklist strings.
Backend persists filter policies per Child.
Child can view the current policy in read-only mode, including last-updated timestamp and who updated it.

requirements.text: Implement alerts for 'excessive use' based on submitted activity vs configured daily limit, and display alerts in both Parent and Child UIs (Child-facing should be supportive and transparent).
acceptanceCriteria: Backend can compute whether a day exceeds the configured limit using submitted activity durations.
Parent dashboard shows alerts and allows marking them as acknowledged.
Child view shows an informational message when limits are exceeded and can optionally submit a 'request more time' note to Parent.

requirements.text: Create an Admin panel that can manage accounts (view users, roles, parent-child links, disable accounts) and view only aggregated metrics (no direct access to child-submitted activity/location content).
acceptanceCriteria: Admin can list all accounts and change roles / disable accounts.
Admin can view aggregate metrics (e.g., total parents, total children, number of pairings, number of check-ins per day) without any per-child content details.
Admin cannot access raw activity/location entries through UI or backend endpoints.

requirements.text: Add an immutable audit log in the backend for sensitive actions (pairing created, schedule changed, filter changed, account disabled), and expose audit log views to Parent (for their linked children) and Admin (aggregate + metadata only).
acceptanceCriteria: Backend records audit events with timestamp, actor principal, action type, and target (child/user id).
Parent can view audit events relevant to their linked children (no hidden events).
Admin can view audit metadata necessary for support, but not child-submitted content.

requirements.text: Add a Transparency & Policies section: supervision disclosure, data handling summary, consent explanation, and a clear statement of non-supported features (no hidden monitoring, no screen mirroring, no remote camera).
acceptanceCriteria: A dedicated page is accessible from footer/header with plain-English disclosures.
The page explicitly states that the web app does not perform covert monitoring, screen mirroring, or remote camera access.
Consent expectations are shown during pairing and within the Child check-in UI.

requirements.text: Establish a coherent, distinct visual theme for the web app (color palette, typography, spacing, components) and apply it consistently across Parent/Child/Admin screens (avoid blue/purple as the primary palette).
acceptanceCriteria: Theme is applied consistently to layouts, buttons, forms, tables, and headings.
Primary palette is not blue/purple (unless used only as minor accents).
UI is responsive and usable on mobile browsers and desktop.

requirements.text: Add generated static images (logo + simple hero illustration) to frontend public assets and use them in the app shell and landing/onboarding screens.
acceptanceCriteria: Images exist under frontend/public/assets/generated and are referenced directly by the frontend.
App shell includes the logo in header/auth screens.
Landing/onboarding uses the hero illustration without fetching it from the backend.

constraints: Backend must remain a single Motoko actor (no additional backend services).
Do not modify files under frontend/src/components/ui or other immutable paths listed in SYSTEM_CONTEXT; compose them instead.
No features that enable covert surveillance (e.g., screen mirroring, remote camera access, hidden notifications suppression).
Do not implement password emailing; authentication must use supported Internet Identity mechanisms and disclose account recovery expectations accordingly.
nonGoals: Building native Android/iOS device monitoring agents.
Real-time screen streaming, keylogging, microphone/camera remote access, or any hidden/stealth monitoring.
Integrations requiring WebSockets/Socket.io/push notifications or external databases/email providers.

required: Minimal shield-and-family logo, flat vector style (pc-logo.dim_256x256.png)
Warm, friendly illustration of a parent and child with a calendar and checklist, flat vector style (pc-hero.dim_1200x600.png)
